hints: Look at the displacement-time graph and find how long one full oscillation takes by comparing two successive peaks at $0 \text{ ns}$ and $10 \text{ ns}$.
Recall that for a displacement-time trace the period $T$ in $\text{ns}$ gives frequency from $f = 1/T$, so convert $\text{ns}$ to $\text{s}$ before comparing to $\text{MHz}$.
Check the displacement scale: the curve reaches $+5 \text{ mm}$ and $-5 \text{ mm}$, so decide whether amplitude is the distance from zero or the distance from trough to crest.
walkthrough: Read the axes: vertical is displacement in $\text{mm}$ with zero in the middle, horizontal is time in $\text{ns}$ from $0$ to $20$.

Find the period $T$ as the time for one complete cycle. The trace starts at a maximum at $t = 0$, returns to a maximum at $t = 10 \text{ ns}$, then repeats to $t = 20 \text{ ns}$, so $T = 10 \text{ ns} = 10 \times 10^{-9} \text{ s} = 1.0 \times 10^{-8} \text{ s}$.
Calculate frequency from $f = 1/T = 1/(1.0 \times 10^{-8} \text{ s}) = 1.0 \times 10^{8} \text{ Hz} = 100 \text{ MHz}$.
Find amplitude as maximum displacement from equilibrium (zero), not peak-to-peak. The peaks are at $+5 \text{ mm}$ and troughs at $-5 \text{ mm}$, so amplitude $= 5 \text{ mm}$.
Combine $100 \text{ MHz}$ and $5 \text{ mm}$. This is option A.
